_about: Field guide for analysis/categories/1.1-former-industrial-service-estates.json: what each field of case_template means, its allowed options, unit, desk source and the paper it comes from. Not filled in.

field_options._format: Every entry: type (one_of | list_of | number | year | text | date | object), definition, options (if any), unit, desk_source (if fillable at the desk), source (paper, page). Blocks follow the order of case_template.
field_options._source: typology v5, section 2 (fields recorded for every site, never used to define a type)
field_options._provenance_for_desk_fields: Fields with a desk_source are tagged source_documented; write the dataset and year in the field's source.

coordinates.definition: WGS84 latitude / longitude of the site centre.

secondary_types.definition: Other sub-types present on the site.

use_history.definition: Earlier uses, oldest first ('use, years'). see analysis/cases/codebook.json

year_built.definition: Year of construction of the main buildings (earliest if several).

sources.definition: One list of every source used for the case. Other fields refer to sources by id (e.g. 'S1, p. 4').

date.definition: Date of the source (or of the image / dataset).

site._definition: Fixed facts about the land that do not change with regeneration. Anything that can change is recorded in before and again in after.

cadastral_ref.definition: Cadastral parcel reference(s) of the site. Site boundary follows parcel boundaries.
cadastral_ref.source: Rebernik et al. 2023, p. 8; Okeyinka et al. 2023, p. 15

parcel_shape.source: Kim et al. 2018, Table 2 (rectangular / irregular / linear)
parcel_shape.note: shape_index gives the same information as a number; parcel_shape is the quick visual class.

shape_index.definition: Shape index = 0.25 × perimeter / √area (1 = square; higher = more irregular). Measured on the site polygon.
shape_index.source: Song et al. 2020, eq. 2; Preston et al. 2023 use similar shape metrics

slope.note: Can be derived from mean_slope_deg (5 % ≈ 2.9°): fill mean_slope_deg, then slope.

mean_slope_deg.definition: Mean slope of the site in degrees, from a digital terrain model.

geology.definition: Soil / ground type under the site and its permeability. permeable = hydraulic conductivity > 10⁻⁴ cm/s; impermeable = < 10⁻⁶ cm/s.
geology.source: Chrysochoou et al. 2012, p. 192; Mahammedi et al. 2021, p. 15; Okeyinka et al. 2023, p. 14

water_proximity_m.definition: Distance in metres from the site edge to the nearest surface water (river, stream, sea, lake).
water_proximity_m.desk_source: Orthophoto + QGIS Measure Line; ICGC hydrography
water_proximity_m.source: Chrysochoou et al. 2012, p. 192; Okeyinka et al. 2023, p. 12 (250 m)

flood_risk.definition: Position of the site relative to mapped flood zones. Write the return period used (e.g. T100) in flood_return_period.
flood_risk.desk_source: ACA flood maps; IDEE WMS riesgos-naturales/inundaciones
flood_risk.source: Chrysochoou et al. 2012, p. 193; Okeyinka et al. 2023, p. 12; Mahammedi et al. 2021, p. 15

flood_return_period.definition: Return period of the flood map used, e.g. T100.

connectivity.definition: Distances in metres from the site edge, measured in QGIS.
connectivity.desk_source: Open Data BCN, TMB stops, OpenStreetMap
connectivity.source: Chrysochoou et al. 2012, p. 191 (bus 402 m, rail 804 m); Okeyinka et al. 2023, pp. 11–13, 18; Rebernik et al. 2023, p. 8

years_vacant.definition: How long the site has been vacant.
years_vacant.note: building unoccupied 60 days (others 120 days or more) = abandoned (Németh & Langhorst 2014, p. 144); empty homes > 6 months = long-term (Madanipour 2017, p. 5)

cause_of_vacancy.definition: Why the site became empty. Choose one main cause; list others in secondary_causes.

options.deindustrialisation: the industry closed down or moved away
options.economic_crisis: a crisis or population decline emptied it
options.leftover_land: land left over from planning, never really used
options.waiting_for_redevelopment: emptied on purpose for a project that stalled
options.excessive_land_division: parcel divided too small to be used economically (Song et al. 2020, §3.4.1)
options.irregular_parcel_shape: parcel shape prevents efficient use (Song et al. 2020, §3.4.2)
options.land_speculation: held empty waiting for land prices to rise (Song et al. 2020, §3.4.4)
options.insufficient_investment: construction stopped or never started for lack of capital (Song et al. 2020, §3.4.4)
options.held_in_reserve: kept vacant by a company or institution for future expansion (Lee & Newman 2019, p. 308)
options.environmental_constraints: contamination, steep slope, flooding or landslide risk (Song et al. 2020, §3.4.4)
options.relocation_of_function: the use moved elsewhere (e.g. offices to a new civic centre) (Madanipour 2017, pp. 3, 8; Bragaglia & Rossignolo 2021, p. 370)
options.planning_blight: the prospect of a planned change stops new investment in the area (Madanipour 2017, p. 3)
options.oversupply: more space was built than demanded (Madanipour 2017, p. 8)
options.disinvestment: withdrawal of investment from an area, incl. historical redlining (Németh & Langhorst 2014, p. 144)
options.suburbanisation: activities and residents moved to the suburbs (Németh & Langhorst 2014, p. 144; Madanipour 2017, p. 3)

cause_of_vacancy.note: First five options from analysis/cases/codebook.json v2; the rest added 12 Nov 2026. relocation_of_function, planning_blight, oversupply, disinvestment, suburbanisation added from Section E. planning_blight differs from waiting_for_redevelopment: no project has started.

secondary_causes.definition: Other causes; same options as cause_of_vacancy.

status.definition: Use status of the site while vacant.
status.note: 'underused' kept, although Németh & Langhorst 2014 (p. 144) do not count underutilised parcels as vacant land.

previous_use_risk.definition: Risk level of the previous use. A = small / general industry, mine spoil heaps; B = garages, workshops, railway lines, textiles, sewage works; C = metal working, scrapyards, shipyards, small gasworks and power stations, rail depots; D = major gasworks, iron and steel, large chemical works, refineries, large power stations, tank farms.

site_layout.definition: clear = clear plot, no obstructions; obstructed = buildings or structures on it; fragmented = split into parts.

enclosure.definition: Whether the site is surrounded by walls or fences.
enclosure.source: Bonthoux et al. 2014, p. 85 (walled sites lower plant richness); Cui et al. 2025, p. 13

vegetation.definition: Vegetation on the site at the time of recording (before: while vacant; after: after regeneration).

fields.ndvi_mean: mean NDVI of the site (−1 to 1), from infrared / multispectral imagery (Bonthoux et al. 2014, p. 85; Cui et al. 2025, p. 14)
fields.vegetation_height_m: mean vegetation height in m, from LiDAR / surface model or site (Bonthoux et al. 2014, p. 85)

vegetation.desk_source: ICGC infrared orthophoto (NDVI) and ICGC LiDAR v1 2008–2011 (height); LiDAR vegetation classes must be masked with NDVI > 0 (roofs misclassified at Can Batlló)
vegetation.note: Kim et al. 2018, Table 2: large canopy > 30 %. Removed 14 Nov 2026: tree count and species count (not automatable from remote data); plantable_space_pct (derived from land_cover_pct, see its note).

land_cover_pct.definition: Share of site area per land-cover class (sums to 100). Measurable from aerial imagery.
land_cover_pct.source: Preston et al. 2023, §2.4 (shadow class excluded); Kim et al. 2018, Table 6 uses a finer list
land_cover_pct.note: Plantable space = 100 − buildings − impervious_surface (Kim et al. 2018, Table 2: large plantable space > 50 %); not stored, derived.

surface_substrate.definition: Main ground substrates on the site (list; one or more).
surface_substrate.desk_source: Orthophoto (close zoom), street-level images; confirm on site
surface_substrate.source: Bonthoux et al. 2014, p. 84; Cui et al. 2025, pp. 8, 11

infrastructure.definition: Utilities on or next to the site (water, sewer, power, telecom).
infrastructure.desk_source: Position in urban fabric; visible roads, pylons, substations on orthophoto
infrastructure.source: Okeyinka et al. 2023, pp. 12, 19; Chrysochoou et al. 2012, p. 191; Rebernik et al. 2023, p. 8

maintenance.definition: Whether the site shows signs of upkeep while vacant.

human_traces.definition: Visible traces of human use or disturbance on the site (list).
human_traces.source: Bonthoux et al. 2014, pp. 83, 85; Cui et al. 2025, pp. 12–13

ownership.definition: Owner type of the site; fragmented = several owners.
ownership.source: Rebernik et al. 2023, pp. 15–16, Fig. 9; Okeyinka et al. 2023, p. 7; owner_behaviour: Lee & Newman 2019, p. 308 (Adams 1994; Dewar & Thomas 2012)
ownership.note: owner_behaviour: active = owner manages or markets the site; passive = owner has stopped managing it or holds it without use.

reuse_cost.definition: Estimated / planned cost of remediation or conversion while vacant.
reuse_cost.source: Lee & Newman 2019, p. 309; Preston et al. 2023, p. 2
reuse_cost.note: The cost of the regeneration that actually happened goes in after.regeneration_cost.

response_to_vacancy.definition: How owners or authorities responded to the vacancy (list).
response_to_vacancy.source: Madanipour 2017, p. 4; Németh & Langhorst 2014, p. 146, Table 2
response_to_vacancy.note: If temporary_use is chosen, fill the temporary block.

zoning.definition: Designated land use / zoning of the site in the current plan. Write as in the plan, with the plan name and year.
zoning.source: Kim et al. 2018, Table 3; Lee & Newman 2019; Song et al. 2020

planning_status.definition: Planning status of redevelopment at the time of recording (terms from the UK register; write the local equivalent in zoning).

surrounding_context.definition: Short description of the surroundings. see analysis/cases/codebook.json

neighbour_sensitivity.definition: low = remote or industrial surroundings; moderate = commercial / retail; high = housing.
neighbour_sensitivity.source: Okeyinka et al. 2023, pp. 13, 19; Chrysochoou et al. 2012, p. 192; Mahammedi et al. 2021, p. 15

nearby_green_spaces.definition: Green spaces around the site (parks, other vacant sites, gardens, river banks), not only protected ones. Give the buffer radius used.
nearby_green_spaces.desk_source: OpenStreetMap, Open Data BCN parks, land-cover map
nearby_green_spaces.source: Bonthoux et al. 2014, p. 85; Cui et al. 2025, pp. 13, 16

surrounding_built_up_pct.definition: Share of buildings / built-up land within the same buffer as nearby_green_spaces (a dispersal barrier).
surrounding_built_up_pct.source: Bonthoux et al. 2014, p. 85; Cui et al. 2025, p. 16

nearest_other_vacant_site_m.definition: Distance in metres to the nearest other vacant site (ecological connectivity).
nearest_other_vacant_site_m.source: Bonthoux et al. 2014, p. 85; Cui et al. 2025, p. 13

surroundings.definition: Conditions in the area around the site in a given year (here: at vacancy / after regeneration), compared with a wider area. Same fields in before and after so the two can be compared.

spatial_unit.definition: Statistical unit of the data: district, neighbourhood, small research zone, census tract.

comparison_area.definition: Wider area used for comparison, e.g. the district.

indicators.note: unemployment_rate in %; population_density in inhabitants / km².

surroundings.desk_source: Open Data BCN (Departament d'Estadística), Catastro; units: district, neighbourhood, small research zone, census tract
surroundings.source: Kim et al. 2018, Table 2; Lee & Newman 2019, Table 1; Song et al. 2020, §3.5; Chrysochoou et al. 2012, pp. 189–190; Anguelovski et al. 2018, pp. 5, 11, 14, 26; Wedding & Crawford-Brown 2007, p. 487; Nocca & Remøy 2026, p. 9 (3.6.d.1–2); Doick et al. 2009, p. 8

type.definition: The actual activity (garden, workspace, events…). see analysis/cases/codebook.json

type_category.definition: Kind of temporary urbanism. Write the actual activity (garden, workspace, events…) in temporary.type.
type_category.source: Bragaglia & Rossignolo 2021, pp. 373–374, Fig. 1; Madanipour 2017, p. 5 (meanwhile use)

start_date.definition: Start of the temporary use: YYYY or YYYY-MM.
start_date.source: Németh & Langhorst 2014, p. 144 (explicitly time-limited); Madanipour 2017, p. 9; Bragaglia & Rossignolo 2021, p. 375

end_date.definition: End of the temporary use: YYYY or YYYY-MM, or "ongoing".

area_pct.definition: Surface used for temporary use as % of total site area.

legal_framework.definition: Legal basis of the temporary use.
legal_framework.source: Németh & Langhorst 2014, p. 147 (sanctioned / unsanctioned); Madanipour 2017, p. 5; Bragaglia & Rossignolo 2021, pp. 375, 378

agreement_type.definition: Type of agreement, e.g. meanwhile lease, temporary concession contract.

visitors_per_year.definition: Number of visitors per year during the temporary use.

user_rent.definition: Rent paid by temporary users: amount, currency, period.

reversibility.definition: no_permanent_change = removable, fully reversible; permanent_changes = buildings altered or removed, pavement removed, topography changed, new structures.

link_to_permanent_plan.definition: Whether a permanent plan for the site exists.
link_to_permanent_plan.source: Bragaglia & Rossignolo 2021, p. 377 (Paris defined, Nantes not); Németh & Langhorst 2014, p. 147

actors.definition: People and organisations involved in this phase.

sector.source: Bragaglia & Rossignolo 2021, pp. 375–376, Figs 2–3; Madanipour 2017, pp. 8–9

role.source: He, Zainol & Azali 2024, pp. 9, 11, Table 6 (14 stakeholder types)

initiator.definition: True if the actor started the temporary use or the regeneration.

assessment.definition: When the after block was recorded, relative to the completion of the new use. The date is that of the most recent source used.

phase.definition: ex_ante = before or during design; ongoing = during works; ex_post = after completion, in use.

assessment.source: Doick et al. 2009, pp. 5, 18; Wedding & Crawford-Brown 2007, p. 493; He et al. 2024, p. 10, Table 5; Kurtoğlu 2026, p. 2; Nocca & Remøy 2026, p. 1; Anguelovski et al. 2018, p. 14

completion_year.definition: Year the new use was completed / opened.
completion_year.source: Doick et al. 2009, p. 27, Table 2; Kurtoğlu 2026, p. 16; Anguelovski et al. 2018, p. 14

new_use.definition: New function(s) after regeneration (list; one or more for mixed use).
new_use.source: Rebernik et al. 2023, p. 5, Table 2; list form: Wedding & Crawford-Brown 2007, p. 487 (number of uses of the site); Kurtoğlu 2026, p. 16

end_use_sensitivity.definition: Sensitivity of the planned or new use. low = commercial / industrial; moderate = public open space, flats; high = housing with gardens, schools, allotments.
end_use_sensitivity.source: Okeyinka et al. 2023, pp. 6–7, 18; Mahammedi et al. 2021, p. 15

retained_fabric.definition: How much of the existing structures was kept.
retained_fabric.desk_source: before / after orthophotos (footprints), plans, project documents
retained_fabric.source: Wedding & Crawford-Brown 2007, p. 487; Nocca & Remøy 2026, p. 12 (6.9.d.1, 6.9.f.2); Kurtoğlu 2026, p. 13 (HCV)

after.site_layout: same as before.site_layout, recorded after regeneration
after.enclosure: same as before.enclosure, recorded after regeneration

land_cover_pct.definition: Same classes as before.land_cover_pct, measured after regeneration (e.g. % of site as green space).
land_cover_pct.source: Wedding & Crawford-Brown 2007, p. 487 (% of site as greenspace); Nocca & Remøy 2026, p. 7 (1.2.g.2)

after.vegetation: same as before.vegetation, recorded after regeneration
after.surface_substrate: same as before.surface_substrate, recorded after regeneration
after.infrastructure: same as before.infrastructure, recorded after regeneration

reclaimed_area_m2.definition: Area of the site brought back into use, m².

gentrification.definition: see analysis/cases/codebook.json Numbers go in surroundings.

governance_type.definition: How the regeneration was led (list; one or more). Details in after.governance.
governance_type.source: Nocca & Remøy 2026, pp. 3, 10; Wedding & Crawford-Brown 2007, p. 493; Anguelovski et al. 2018, pp. 9–10; He et al. 2024, p. 12; Doick et al. 2009, p. 5

governance.definition: Description of how the regeneration was led; people and organisations go in actors. see analysis/cases/codebook.json

regeneration_cost.definition: Documented cost of regeneration / conversion. Leave null if not published.
regeneration_cost.source: Doick et al. 2009, p. 27, Table 2 (£ and £/ha); Wedding & Crawford-Brown 2007, p. 487; Kurtoğlu 2026, p. 20; Nocca & Remøy 2026, p. 9 (3.6.f.1–2)

jobs_created.definition: Jobs generated by the new use, if published. Leave null if not.
jobs_created.source: Wedding & Crawford-Brown 2007, p. 487 (net jobs per acre); Nocca & Remøy 2026, p. 10 (4.7.a.1)
jobs_created.note: Wedding & Crawford-Brown 2007, p. 493: jobs per acre depends on the future use and may not track success.

community_objections.definition: Documented objections or support from residents (e.g. in planning records, press).
community_objections.source: Madanipour 2017, p. 9; Okeyinka et al. 2023, p. 14; Chrysochoou et al. 2012, p. 197

actors.definition: People and organisations involved in this phase.

sector.source: Bragaglia & Rossignolo 2021, pp. 375–376, Figs 2–3; Madanipour 2017, pp. 8–9

role.source: He, Zainol & Azali 2024, pp. 9, 11, Table 6 (14 stakeholder types)

initiator.definition: True if the actor started the temporary use or the regeneration.

after.zoning: same as before.zoning, recorded after regeneration
after.nearby_green_spaces: same as before.nearby_green_spaces, recorded after regeneration
after.surrounding_built_up_pct: same as before.surrounding_built_up_pct, recorded after regeneration

provenance._definition: Per block of the case. tag = how the block was filled; evidence_status = how well it is supported; field_notes = per-field exceptions (e.g. 'after.jobs_created': 'not_available').

evidence_status.definition: documented = supported by a source; provisional = partly supported; not_available = no evidence, field left empty (not scored as zero).
evidence_status.source: Kurtoğlu 2026, p. 10 (NA, provisional), p. 19 (Table 8 evidence status)
evidence_status.note: Kurtoğlu's Table 7 also uses evidence levels A / B / C; their definitions were not found in the text, so they are not used here.

sub_types._definition: Fields inside each sub-type (category level, not per case).

typical_objects.definition: Objects commonly found in this sub-type (e.g. gas holders in 1.1.c). One entry per object, using this template.
typical_objects.note: Object classes and materials: see analysis/categories/objects-codebook.json → object

ground_constraints.definition: Ground hazards commonly found in this sub-type (e.g. contaminated soil, buried foundations, old tanks); kept apart from objects because they are risks, not reusable material. One entry per constraint, using this template.

not_in_json_need_site_visit_or_expert: tree count per ha and tree species count (removed 14 Nov 2026; Kim et al. 2018, Table 2; not automatable from remote data)
ecosystem services (stormwater, heat island, air quality)
visitor satisfaction, place attachment and perceived safety surveys
structural safety, fire and MEP reports
visitors per year after reuse (not added, 13 Nov 2026)
nearby protected areas, Natura 2000 (removed 13 Nov 2026; Chrysochoou et al. 2012, p. 193; Okeyinka partial)
